messages:
Megan: Quick proposal — tweak spot-backed autoscaler to use dynamic cooldown + surge gating to avoid churn during region-level evictions. want to run a canary.
Arun: +1. what metric will trigger scale-out? avg GPU utilization or queue depth?
Megan: primary trigger = 75% GPU util sustained for 30s or queue depth > 250 requests/s for 15s. prefer util for steady-state, queue for spikes.
Lucia: curious about cooldown logic — static 60s doesn't cut it when spot churn happens.
Megan: agreed. idea: cooldown = base 60s * (1 + eviction_rate_window / 0.1). so if eviction rate is 20%, cooldown doubles.
Toni: also should gate surge by available on-demand capacity. we don't want surges that push cost through roof.
Megan: exactly — surge_allowed = min(15%, on_demand_capacity_pct). reserve_spot_pool = 10% to absorb small evictions.
James: can you paste the canary config? want to review before deploy.
Megan: here's the canary snippet:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  scale_out:
    metric: gpu_util
    threshold: 0.75
    window_seconds: 30
  queue_trigger:
    metric: request_qps
    threshold: 250
    window_seconds: 15
  cooldown:
    base_seconds: 60
    dynamic_formula: "base_seconds * (1 + eviction_rate / 0.1)"
  surge_control:
    max_surge_pct: 0.15
    require_on_demand_budget: true
  reserve_spot_pool_pct: 10
  preemption_hedge: true
```
Arun: Nice. how do we compute eviction_rate? rolling 5m of spot preempt events / spot_count?
Megan: rolling 5m, yes. weighted by region. if us-east has high eviction rate we scale regionally and increase cooldowns there.
autoscaler-bot: Canary deployment started in us-west-2 at 1973460000. canary id: canary-2026-03-18-01
Lucia: i'd add a safety gate: if observed p50 latency goes up > 20% during canary, abort and rollback automatically.
Megan: good call — adding latency regression gate tied to our eval prompt set.
Toni: what's the expected cost delta for allowing 15% surge + 10% reserve? rough ballpark.
James: rough calc: baseline spot cost X, adding 10% reserve ~ +10% cost, allowing up to 15% surge could add another ~12% during heavy periods. net worst-case ~+22% but should reduce error budget overruns.
Megan: tradeoff is fewer failed requests and less retry storms causing even higher egress costs. net might be neutral or slightly positive.
ops-bot: FYI — past 30d average spot evictions in eu-west-1 jumped from 2% -> 8% during week of 1973380000.
Arun: For mixed pools, allocation order should be: warm-on-demand -> reserve-spot -> spot. ensures we don't instantly kill on-demand when spot returns.
Megan: yes, config will prefer warm on-demand with preemptible hedge as a fallback. also add per-region soft limits so one noisy region doesn't deplete global on-demand quota.
James: timeline? canary 48h in us-west-2; if stable, roll to us-east and eu-west gradually.
Megan: deploying canary now. will monitor eviction_rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and cost delta. will post hourly updates.
Lucia: thanks — i'll wire the latency gate into the rollback hook.
Megan: thanks all. if anything odd ping me or @on-call.
autoscaler-bot: Canary canary-2026-03-18-01 metrics stream: https://metrics.internal/canary-2026-03-18-01
James: ack, will check in 1h. :thumbsup: "
